name: Comfort Systems USA, Inc.
monetization: Installs the mechanical and electrical guts of data centers — HVAC, piping, modular builds, electrical — with technology customers now ~58% of revenue and a record $14.1B backlog.
description_md: Comfort Systems USA is a national mechanical and electrical contractor (HVAC, plumbing, piping, controls, and electrical services, plus off-site modular construction) that has become one of the purest listed plays on data-center construction labor. Technology customers — dominated by data centers for hyperscale cloud providers — supplied 58.7% of Q2 2026 revenue, and the backlog of $14.1B (+73% y/y) is primarily technology-driven. Its modular/off-site fabrication capability is a differentiator in compressing hyperscaler build timelines.
ai_monetization_md: AI monetizes as construction billings: Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $3.27B (+50% y/y) with net income up 91% to $441.6M, driven by data-center mechanical and electrical work. New construction was 75.1% of revenue. Like Quanta, Comfort Systems is paid for skilled labor and execution rather than equipment, so its results track physical buildout activity directly — and its 73% backlog growth is among the strongest demand signals in the construction tier. The company holds a net cash position above $1.8B, funding acquisitions and buybacks.
ai_strategy_md: Concentrate where the labor shortage bites: keep winning hyperscale data-center mechanical/electrical scopes, expand modular off-site construction (which economizes scarce field labor), and roll up regional specialty contractors with the balance-sheet room its net cash provides. Management leans into technology-sector mix rather than diversifying away from it.
risk_notes_md: Customer and end-market concentration: ~58% of revenue from technology/data centers means an AI construction pause would hit revenue and the multiple simultaneously — backlog can be re-phased by the same few hyperscale customers who drove it up. Skilled-labor availability limits growth and raises wage-inflation risk on fixed-price work. The stock's re-rating embeds continuation of 50%-class revenue growth that is historically anomalous for a mechanical contractor.

observations.notes: Next largest: manufacturing 16.4%, healthcare 7.1%. Technology is overwhelmingly data-center construction.
